clue.text: Man at home is excited getting it

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters before it are thrown about

blocks.note: the nine letters of these three words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A man left alone at home gets excited about something, perhaps finally understanding it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden flash of understanding is the instant of finally grasping something, so the phrase stands for that point of comprehension.

clue.text: A sailor grips top of weapon when fighting

indicators.note: to grip is to hold something tight, so one piece clasps another inside it
in a down clue the top of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
tar is an old word for a seaman
the first letter of weapon

explanation.surface: A sailor clutches the end of his weapon in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The W sits inside TAR, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Two nations engaged in conflict are said to be in a state of hostilities, so the phrase describes the condition of combat.

clue.text: Friendly question about setter's competence?

blocks.note: the setter, speaking as I, asks whether they have the capacity, in three short words

explanation.surface: A friendly inquiry into whether the crossword setter is any good.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AM I ABLE, the word is the setter asking if they are up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amiable is good-natured and pleasant company, the same warm disposition as being friendly.

clue.text: Old poet repulsed male singer

indicators.note: something repulsed is driven back, so in this down clue the word is pushed upward and read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a divo is the male counterpart of a diva, a celebrated singer

explanation.surface: An ancient poet was disgusted by a male vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman author of the Metamorphoses lived two thousand years ago, a classical verse writer from antiquity.

clue.text: Investment insurance lacking hard limit

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the word loses what follows it

blocks.note: a hedge is a position taken to protect against losses on an investment
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A financial safeguard on investments that has no firm ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The boundary or brink of something marks where it stops, the same idea as its outermost bound.

clue.text: Whisky measure is an insult

blocks.note: first meaning: a generous pour judged by finger widths in the glass
second meaning: the rude British V-sign made with the hand

explanation.surface: Being served a stingy measure of whisky feels like an affront.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the V-sign made with the back of the hand outward is an obscene gesture of contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinkers gauge spirits by finger widths in a glass, and the British two-digit gesture is a rude rebuff.

clue.text: Central area owners vowed to make fresh again

indicators.note: the central part of each following word is kept and the outer letters dropped

blocks.note: the two middle letters of a four-letter word
the two middle letters of a six-letter word
the single middle letter of a five-letter word

explanation.surface: Landlords in the middle of town promise to revitalise the place.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to restore it or replace it so that it is as good as new once more.

clue.text: It's OK following procedure that guarantees passage

definitions.note: a relative clause standing in for the noun: something that guarantees passage

blocks.note: saying that's right confirms something is OK
of in the sense of after the fashion of, i.e. following
a way of doing something is a method or procedure

explanation.surface: Reassurance that sticking to the correct process will get you through.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal entitlement to cross land, or to proceed first in traffic, ensures that a person may go through.

clue.text: Unload bananas with burst centre getting lumpy

indicators.note: going bananas means going crazy, so the letters are scrambled
the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter alone

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle letter of burst

explanation.surface: Unpacking a bunch of bananas whose middles have split leaves them misshapen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nodular is covered in small knobs or swellings, so its texture is knobbly and uneven.

clue.text: Moderate report on reservoir after drought?

definitions.note: a cryptic second definition: a news line saying levels have fallen

blocks.note: first meaning: to dilute or make less forceful, as with a proposal
second meaning: a headline announcing that a reservoir's level has fallen

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the phrase is just what a reservoir bulletin would say after a dry summer; as a phrasal verb it means to weaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute a plan or statement is to tone it down and soften its force, the sense of moderate as a verb.

clue.text: Didn't remember to retain act after delaying play

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so the first word keeps another within it

blocks.note: delaying and waiting both mean holding off
the past tense of failing to recall
to do is to act

explanation.surface: An absent-minded actor forgot to keep his part in a stalled production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' looks like a theatre noun, but it is a verb here. Beckett's play is famous for a title character who never arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett's celebrated absurdist drama, in which two tramps wait for someone who never turns up, is a stage work.

clue.text: Supports I invested in troubled financial institution, initially

indicators.note: money invested in a firm is put inside it, so the letter is placed within the other piece

blocks.note: the initials of the Royal Bank of Scotland, bailed out by the British government in 2008
taken as written

explanation.surface: Backing money put into a bank in trouble, at the start of the crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: RBS, the Royal Bank of Scotland, needed a huge state rescue in the 2008 financial crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved bones of the chest, or curved timbers of a boat's hull, hold up and give the frame its strength.

clue.text: Tube-like shape is artful?

indicators.note: to shape something is to mould it into a new form, so the letters after it are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a tubular form counts as clever design.
explanation.definitionFit: A fistula is a pipe or narrow passage in the body, so the adjective means hollow and pipe-shaped.

clue.text: Weak sister exercised to get warmer on the slopes

indicators.note: something exercised has been worked and moved about, so the letters are put through their paces

blocks.note: the letters of both words, taken as written

explanation.surface: A feeble sibling works out to keep warm on a winter holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warmer' reads as a comparative adjective but is a noun: a garment that warms you.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick knitted pullover worn by skiers keeps the body heated while on snowy mountain runs.

clue.text: Carefree group talking nonsense

blocks.note: blithe means happy and without worry
a ring is a group of people, often a criminal one

explanation.surface: A happy-go-lucky bunch chattering away about nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To blither is to babble foolishly, so someone doing it is prattling on without sense.

clue.text: Good luck to player from a supporter on holiday

blocks.note: a break is a short holiday
taken as written
a leg holds up a table or a body

explanation.surface: A fan away on holiday sends a message wishing a sportsman well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests sport, but here it is an actor, to whom saying 'good luck' is thought unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre superstition forbids wishing actors success directly, so this idiom is the customary substitute before a performance.

clue.text: Club Med, for example, found in south London

definitions.note: describes a district rather than naming it: a place found there

blocks.note: to club someone is to beat them repeatedly
the Mediterranean is a sea

explanation.surface: A Club Med resort turns up somewhere improbable in south London.
explanation.walkthrough: Club Med is a holiday-resort brand, but the words split into a verb and an example of a body of water; Battersea is a London district south of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The area known for its power station and dogs' home lies on the south bank of the Thames in the capital.

clue.text: Give up position of a Brexiter?

blocks.note: a Brexiter is in favour of the UK going out of the EU

explanation.surface: Asking whether a supporter of leaving the EU would be willing to back down.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FOR GO, it is the stance of someone backing Britain's departure from the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to do without it or relinquish it voluntarily, the same as surrendering it.

clue.text: Spain's answer to pasta bake?

indicators.note: baking transforms ingredients, so the letters are cooked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering what the Spanish equivalent of an Italian oven dish would be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: rework the Italian staple and you get the Spanish one.
explanation.definitionFit: Small savoury dishes served with drinks are Spain's signature food, as pasta dishes are Italy's.

clue.text: Anticipate temper cracking under pressure

indicators.note: something cracking breaks apart, so the letters fall into a new order
in a down clue, under means placed below, so the scrambled letters follow the other piece

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: Foreseeing someone losing their cool when the pressure is on.
explanation.definitionFit: To act ahead of an expected event in order to forestall it is to see it coming and get in first.

clue.text: Cover fool returned, saying it's completely knackered

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
saying means speaking, so the next words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: prat is British slang for an idiot
all in is British slang for exhausted, and knackered means worn out

explanation.surface: A clumsy oaf comes back and announces he is utterly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAT backwards gives TARP; 'knackered' is British slang for exhausted, i.e. all in, which is said like the ending AULIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy waterproof canvas sheet is laid over goods or equipment to protect them from rain.

clue.text: She contributes to article on Orangism

indicators.note: the name is a contributor to the words that follow, part of them rather than whole

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A woman writes for a piece about the Orange Order.
explanation.walkthrough: Orangism is the Protestant loyalist movement of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's given name, as in Beethoven's heroine, so a female pronoun can point to it.

clue.text: Centre with flat, where pupils are situated

definitions.note: a place description: the height of the eyes

blocks.note: the eye of a storm is its centre
level means even, without slopes

explanation.surface: A centre that comes with an apartment, where schoolchildren are based.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupils' suggests schoolchildren; here they are the dark centres of the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The height at which one's eyes sit is where the openings of the iris are found, so the phrase is pupil height.

clue.text: Class make simplistic gender choice

blocks.note: the two-box option on a questionnaire

explanation.surface: A school class is asked to fill in a tick-box sex question.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes: a school year group, to create, and the binary box on official paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools a year group is called this, and the verb also means to shape or create something.

clue.text: City where furry animals have their tails up!

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the tail up means the final pair of letters is flipped upward

blocks.note: minks are small furry mammals prized for their pelts

explanation.surface: A town where the fluffy creatures carry their tails high in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the last two letters of the animals are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Belarus is a large Eastern European metropolis, a city in plain dictionary sense.

clue.text: Look hard at long clue that's oddly deficient

indicators.note: lacking its odd-numbered letters, so only the even positions remain

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Staring at a lengthy clue that is strangely lacking something.
explanation.definitionFit: To leer or gaze greedily at someone is to stare at them intently and openly.

clue.text: Henchman boarded without ticket stub

indicators.note: without means going lacking, so a letter is removed
a stub is a small remaining piece, here just the start of the word

blocks.note: boarded a bus or train means got on it
the first letter of ticket

explanation.surface: A gangster's heavy got on a train without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired thug who does a boss's dirty work is a strong-arm man, the same role as a criminal's muscle.

clue.text: Potty clue?

blocks.note: surface reading: a mad or crazy crossword clue
setter's reading: a child's potty is a seat to use, and a clue is a lead to follow up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like an adjective meaning daft, but it is the child's toilet; both it and a clue are things to proceed with, in different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue gives investigators a lead to pursue, and a toddler's potty is literally a seat used for the toilet.

clue.text: One who perhaps leads as cast take over rehearsals

definitions.text: One who perhaps leads as cast take over rehearsals

indicators.note: leads are the front runners, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: A performer who may have a starring role once the company starts rehearsing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, while its last five words supply their first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer in a play may well take a starring part once the company is cast and rehearsing.

clue.text: Inexperienced defender makes money in the States

blocks.note: green means new to something, naive
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: A novice defender earns a fortune playing in America.
explanation.definitionFit: American dollar bills are printed in green ink on the reverse, giving the slang name for US currency.
